question: Who was the first Sultan of the Sultanate period who arranged for the translation of Hindu scriptures from Sanskrit to Persian?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Firoz Shah Tughlaq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq** was a Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty who ruled over the Delhi Sultanate from **1351 to 1388**.
 
• He was known for his administrative reforms and public works, including the construction of canals, roads, and new cities.
 
• Firoz Shah Tughlaq arranged for the translation of several important **Hindu scriptures** from **Sanskrit to Persian**, making them accessible to a broader audience.
 
• His translations included texts like the **Mahabharata** and other significant works of Hindu literature.
 
• This initiative was part of his broader policy of promoting cultural and religious tolerance within his kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**__

 __
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** was the second ruler of the Khilji dynasty and ruled from **1296 to 1316**.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and economic reforms, including market regulation and price control measures.
 
• He did not focus on cultural or religious translations during his reign.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq**__
 __
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughluq** was a Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty who ruled from **1325 to 1351**.
 
• He is known for his ambitious projects and eccentric policies, such as the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.
 
• He did not arrange for the translation of Hindu scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Sikandar Khan Lodi**__
 
 
• **Sikandar Khan Lodi** was the Sultan of Delhi from **1489 to 1517**.
 
• He was known for his efforts to expand the Lodi Empire and his patronage of Persian literature and culture.
 
• He did not arrange for the translation of Hindu scriptures from Sanskrit to Persian.
